title: IV vinorelbine for platinum-refractory ovarian cancer
schedule_label: IV vinorelbine on days 1 and 8 of a 21-day cycle. Week three is a break. Your team reviews benefit and tolerability before repeating the cycle.
schedule_summary: IV vinorelbine on days 1 and 8 of a 21-day cycle. Week three is a break. Your team reviews benefit and tolerability before repeating the cycle.
purpose: Vinorelbine is being offered to slow the growth of platinum-refractory advanced ovarian cancer. Your team will review symptoms and scan results with you to decide whether to continue.
indication_text: Advanced ovarian carcinoma that is refractory to platinum. This use of IV vinorelbine is unlicensed in Ireland.
administration_text: The nurse gives vinorelbine into a vein over 15 minutes and then flushes the line with saline. Tell them immediately if the site stings, burns or swells.
monitoring_summary: Blood count, kidney and liver tests and assessment of numbness, tingling or weakness. Before each cycle: blood count, kidney and liver tests and neuropathy review. The day-8 dose depends on blood counts and how you are feeling. Symptoms and imaging according to your consultant’s plan.
review_status: Independent oncology, pharmacy and patient review pending.

agents.name: Vinorelbine
agents.mechanism: Disrupts the machinery of cell division
agents.explanation: Vinorelbine disrupts the tiny structures a cell needs to divide. This can stop cancer cells multiplying. Healthy blood-forming cells, gut cells and nerves can also be affected.
agents.watch: Use the treating unit’s 24-hour emergency number and local fever threshold. Contact immediately for fever/chills, sudden illness, breathlessness/chest pain, uncontrolled vomiting, severe abdominal pain/obstruction symptoms, bleeding or severe allergy. Do not wait until the next visit.
risks: Low blood counts, infection and bleeding
Nerve effects and uncommon lung/heart toxicity
consent_risks: Constipation can be severe. Use the bowel plan agreed with your team and report abdominal pain or swelling.
Tingling, weakness or fatigue can affect daily tasks. Tell the team before your next dose.
Low white cells can lead to serious infection. Call immediately for fever or chills.
Severe constipation with cramping, vomiting or swelling needs urgent review.
Vinorelbine can injure surrounding tissue. Tell the nurse immediately about burning, pain or swelling.

anatomy: White blood cells can fall, raising the risk of infection. Anaemia can cause tiredness or breathlessness; low platelets can cause bruising or bleeding. Blood tests guide delays and dose changes. Fever, shaking chills or feeling suddenly unwell need the oncology emergency contact immediately.

The bowel can slow down and nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea or sore mouth can occur. Use the prescribed bowel and anti-sickness plan. Severe abdominal pain, swelling, repeated vomiting or inability to pass stool/gas needs urgent assessment for ileus; do not simply take extra laxatives.
Nerve effects may change sensation, grip, walking or bowel movement. Report changes early because the next dose may need to wait or be reduced.
Tiredness, hair thinning/loss and liver-test changes can occur. Pace activities and tell the team if eating, drinking or daily tasks become difficult.
New chest pain, sudden or worsening breathlessness, or severe allergic symptoms need urgent medical help. Previous heart disease and interacting medicines need review before treatment.
Tell staff immediately about burning, pain, swelling or leakage.
anatomy_note: Use the 24-hour oncology number on your contact card.

questions.q: What should I check before treatment?
questions.a: Tell the team about constipation, numbness and any infection. Confirm your blood test and day-8 appointment before leaving.

questions.q: What should I watch for at home?
questions.a: Record bowel movements and any new tingling. Call promptly for severe constipation, abdominal swelling, vomiting or inability to pass wind.

evidence.title: Phase II study of vinorelbine in platinum-resistant ovarian cancer
evidence.interpretation: Investigators observed tumour responses with single-agent vinorelbine on days 1 and 8.
evidence.limitations: The study included a broader platinum-resistant population and had no control group. It cannot estimate benefit specifically for an individual with platinum-refractory disease.
